basis: Autoimmunity defines this heterogeneous umbrella; no anatomical axis is established across most patients.

decisions.pulmonary: none: upper-airway disease occurs in selected subtypes; common airway damage across the umbrella is not established.
decisions.otologic: none: inner-ear disease is one subtype; ear involvement is not established across most patients.

basis: Developmental impairment and skeletal malformations characterize distal 4q deletion; heart defects affect ~40-50%, cleft palate roughly one-third, varying with deletion extent.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate affects roughly one-third and directly represents oral structural malformation; frequency is near the threshold.

basis: Defining craniofacial skeletal and limb malformations; obstructive choanal atresia, CNS malformations and cardiac defects are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.pulmonary: none: external nasal shape and nasal-bone dysplasia do not establish airway dysfunction; choanal atresia occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Enteric duplication; respiratory insufficiency, cord malformations and rib defects each annotated 80-99%. Cardiac malformations (80-99%) omitted by cap; hepatomegaly alone is not damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: valve malformations are annotated 80-99%, but omitted by cap in favor of respiratory functional loss and spinal/rib malformations.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: respiratory insufficiency is annotated 80-99%; thoracic duplication directly compromises respiratory function through compression.
decisions.neurologic: involved: meningocele and diastematomyelia are annotated 80-99%; associated cord malformations are additional to the defining enteric lesion.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: rib defects are annotated 80-99%, and vertebral malformations are frequent associated structural abnormalities.

basis: Mitochondrial myopathy and cataracts define the disorder; developmental delay/callosal hypoplasia occur in 30-79%. Hearing loss (30-79%) omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay and callosal hypoplasia are frequent (30-79%); developmental and structural CNS impairment merits retention under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: progressive hearing loss qualifies at 30-79%, but is omitted by the four-axis cap in favor of CNS developmental and structural impairment.

basis: Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the syndrome; limb and chest-wall malformations occur in 80-99%. Sparse hair and obesity do not establish additional organ dysfunction.

decisions.dermatologic: none: sparse hair (80-99%) is a dysmorphic finding without established damaging skin or follicular disease.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: truncal obesity (80-99%) alone does not establish direct endocrine or metabolic organ dysfunction from this syndrome.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: syndactyly, pectus excavatum and diaphragmatic malformation are annotated 80-99%; skeletal involvement accompanies the defining neurodevelopmental disorder.

basis: Skin blistering; oral blisters 3/3, developmental delay and hearing impairment each 1/1. Small denominators limit certainty; skeletal findings omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay is explicitly annotated in 1/1 assessed patient; provisionally accept the supplied frequency, with uncertainty from the small sample.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment represents functional loss and is annotated in 1/1 assessed patient; prevalence remains uncertain because of the small sample.

basis: Primary skeletal dysplasia; conductive hearing loss is common across OPD and frontometaphyseal forms, estimated >=30% across the spectrum. Cleft palate is subtype-dependent.

decisions.otologic: involved: conductive hearing loss from ossicular abnormalities is common across several major spectrum disorders, supporting an estimated frequency of at least ~30%.

basis: Defining facial skin/subcutis atrophy; mandibular abnormalities 80-99%, muscle abnormalities 30-79%, and seizures 30-79% in supplied HPO. Ocular findings are occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: bone and muscle atrophy extend beyond the defining skin/subcutis disease; mandibular abnormalities occur in 80-99% and muscle abnormalities in 30-79%.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency defined by near absence of T lymphocytes and NK cells; secondary infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the definition specifies profound deficiency of T lymphocytes and NK blood cells, meeting the explicit blood-cell disease rule.
